name: UT-Austin TRIGA hot channel, 24.34 kW, with the zirconium fill rod (compare with SAR Figure 4.30)
label: sourced
citation: University of Texas TRIGA II SAR, Chapter 4 (8/2023): geometry Table 4.1 (fuel diameter 1.435 in = 3.6322 cm, cladding thickness 0.020 in, outer diameter 1.475 in, fuel length 38.10 cm), fuel conductivity 0.18 W/cm/K (Table 4.1), 304 stainless steel cladding k 16.6 W/m/K at 400 K (K-State SAR Table 4.6, same alloy), hot channel power 24.34 kW (section 4.6) with element axial peaking 1.017 (Table 4.17) over 0.381 m: q' = 24.34 kW / 0.381 m x 1.017 = 64.97 kW/m. READ FROM FIGURE 4.30 (TRACE output, digitized, docs/sources/ut-triga-fig-4.30.json): the cladding outer surface temperature 132.9 C is the boundary here, and the effective gap conductance 4096 W/m2/K is the fuel-surface heat flux over the 139.0 K gap drop in that figure (295.1 C to 156.1 C). Both are therefore outputs of the SAR's TRACE model used as inputs; the comparison below tests only the conduction in the fuel and cladding. The central hole is the 6.35 mm (0.25 in) zirconium fill rod, marked at 0.125 in radius in Figure 4.30; it is modelled as a hole with an insulated surface (no heat conducted into the rod).
description: The same comparison as the solid-cylinder case, with the zirconium fill rod modelled as an insulated central hole (annular fuel). FEED's hottest point (the hole surface) is 544.7 C against the figure's 562.5 C (18 K below); the solid-cylinder model gives 576.3 C (14 K above), so the figure lies between the two models. The shape of the digitized profile favours the annulus (rms 4.7 K against 8.4 K for a solid cylinder). With the SAR's power (65.0 kW/m) the annular fit asks for an effective fuel conductivity of about 17.0 W/m/K instead of 18, i.e. TRACE's U-ZrH conductivity is probably about 6% lower than the Table 4.1 value used here; this is an inference from a digitized figure, not something the SAR states. A comparison case, not an oracle. Thermal only.
